registered: 2026-08-18, BEFORE extracting cell histograms or fitting any dispersion
why: cell-MAE is a MEAN-based ruler: blurring always reduces it, so it cannot discriminate superposition-as-physics from superposition-as-smoother. Measured 2026-08-18: widening blur improved MAE monotonically (0.2808->0.2704) while between-cell spread COLLAPSED (0.71->0.51).

new_ruler.metric: Wasserstein-1 between the engine's within-cell stance density and the REAL within-cell answer density (WVS7 individual responses, survey-weighted, ordinal scale binned identically)
new_ruler.why_it_discriminates: a density that flattens toward uniform pays an immediate penalty; a density that reproduces real bimodality wins. Blurring is no longer free.

readouts_compared: SOFT+ per-agent answer distribution (dispersion FITTED from data, not swept)

BORN coherence readout P=R_yes^2/(R_yes^2+R_no^2) recovered from the old TS engine (cannot be won by blurring: collapsing spread drives both camps' R together and P toward 0.5, which the distributional scorer punishes)

REGISTERED PREDICTIONS.primary: SOFT+ with data-fitted dispersion beats HARD on Wasserstein-1 AND matches observed within-cell spread (ratio 0.8-1.2).
REGISTERED PREDICTIONS.failure_branch_1: matches spread but loses on distance => the shape is wrong even at the right width
REGISTERED PREDICTIONS.failure_branch_2: wins on distance by collapsing spread => still a smoother; superposition rejected on this substrate
REGISTERED PREDICTIONS.born_readout: no registered expectation — first measurement of it on real cell densities

discipline: dispersion is FIT from real within-cell disagreement, never swept to taste; all cell coordinates (age, education) are gate-clean non-benchmark variables.
